title: Star formation fireworks in Orion
caption: Herbig-Haro 502 in the Orion Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Herbig-Haro 502, Orion Nebula · constellation Orion · about 1500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The whole frame is filled with the colorful glow of the Orion Nebula. Just left of center, a star sits in a pinkish haze, and a narrow pink jet reaches away from it, with curved shock fronts to the upper right and lower left. This is the area around Herbig-Haro 502, a tiny piece of a vast stellar nursery.

The star is very young and still wrapped in the gas cloud it formed from. That leftover material may one day build planets. The material of our own Earth probably sat in a similar cocoon about five billion years ago.

The jet and arcs are the Herbig-Haro object. Newborn stars fling out gas at hundreds of kilometers per second, and where it strikes surrounding gas and dust it forms glowing shocks. These are thought to fade after a few thousand years, though they are often much larger than our Solar System.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.23 x 3.19 arcminutes) and distance (1500 light years), the frame spans roughly 1.4 × 1.4 light-years. Its light set out about 1,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys used filters for glowing hydrogen (F658N, red), ionized oxygen (F502N, green) and yellow light (F550W, blue).
understand.eye: Narrowband filters isolate individual gases and exposures of up to 2000 seconds gather far more light than the eye, so the colors are a scientific mapping rather than the view in an eyepiece.

explore: At only around 1500 light-years away, the Orion Nebula is one of the nearest star-forming regions to us. Young stars wrapped in their birth clouds are considered important enough that much Hubble observing time has been devoted to them, and studying them helps explain how the Universe developed and is still changing.
alt: A colorful glowing nebula with a young star in a pink haze left of center and a narrow pink jet with curved shock fronts.
